recall.a: Two-part stories; system-as-actor; header with zero or two primary actors; preconditions confused with triggers; flows that narrate actor-actor talk; generic extensions; diagrams drawn as flowcharts.
recall.q: List six requirements mark-losers from memory.

sections.heading: How requirements marks are lost
bullets: User story missing its benefit clause, or written for 'the system' instead of a user.
Header with no primary actor, two primary actors, or an external system as primary actor.
Flow that describes actor-to-actor conversation the system never mediates.
Extension that is generic ('database fails') instead of scenario-specific with ID, handling and outcome.
Use-case diagram drawn as a flowchart with arrows between ovals.

summary: Six classic requirements mark-losers, from two-part stories to flowchart-diagrams.
title: Requirements: common exam mistakes

distractor.0: The slides' warning slide exists precisely because this is tempting: diagrams map who-does-what, flows carry sequence.

activities.explanation: False — that confusion is an instant mark-loser. Sequencing lives in the written flow; ovals never chain into flowcharts.
